newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara says hasn't retracted newspaper comment.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara says hasn't retracted newspaper comment.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said early on Friday that he has not retracted his comment, quoted in a Japanese newspaper report on Thursday, that the dollar's correction from last year's sharp slide against the yen was about to end.
He made the comment to Reuters while leaving his office following a day in which the new Japanese cabinet was formed.
He also said Japan's position concerning foreign exchange rates has not changed.

Asked about market rumours that he had retracted his comment, which was carried in the Nikkei Financial Daily on Thursday, Sakakibara said: "I haven't retracted it (the comment). But Japan's position concerning forex is unchanged."
Senior Japanese government officials have recently said the dollar was still in the process of an orderly reversal.

Wataru Kubo, then finance minister, said last week: "Current foreign exchange movements are part of a big trend which emerged when G7 leaders agreed last April to work to correct this (the dollar's weakness) through close cooperation and coordination between them in the currency market."
A new finance minister, Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, was named on Thursday following the re-election by parliament of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto. -- Yoko Kobayashi +81-3-3432-8478
